name: LME49713
tagline: Current-feedback single: 1.9 nV/√Hz, 0.00036% THD+N, 1900 V/µs, ±100 mA. A quiet, muscular headphone and buffer stage.

lineage.note: LME49xxx audio line with LME49710/20/40. Released 2007-09; reportedly on National's LME high-voltage process.
Acquired National 2011-09; reissued SNAS386F in 2013-03. Last-time buy expired 2017-11-02; no PDN number found.

part_numbers.note: Generic device name; status per distributor listings.
TO-99 metal can, lead-free; Digi-Key 296-41515-ND. LTB expired 2017-11-02; brokers/LCSC still list.
TO-99 metal can, National-era code before /NOPB.
SOIC-8 lead-free: MA/NOPB in rails, LME49713MAX/NOPB on tape and reel.

key_specs.value: 132 MHz bandwidth (CFB: set by feedback resistor)

reputation.summary: A niche enthusiast favourite. Head-Fi titled a thread 'LME49713, could be a killer opamp'. A diyAudio poster who worked on the chip called it the best-sounding op-amp on National's LME process, preferred to voltage-feedback parts in listening tests. A Head-Fi user found it 'dead silent and with real drive' into 150 Ω. Fast and tricky to stabilise.
typical_uses: Headphone amp or output buffer (drives 150 Ω)
DAC output and I/V stages on SOIC-to-DIP adapters
Make-up gain for passive summing mixers (RMS Folcrom)
caveats: Single, SOIC-8 or TO-99 only: needs a DIP-8 adapter; not a drop-in for dual NE5532/LME49720.
Current feedback: feedback resistor sets bandwidth and stability; no capacitor across it. VFB circuits may oscillate.
diyAudio: ran hot or oscillated in a Sony CDP-557ESD's NE5534 sockets, where an AD844 worked.
About 1.8 µA input bias current can cause large offsets with high-value bias resistors.
Obsolete since the 2017 last-time buy; only old stock and brokers remain.

counterfeit_notes: No LME49713-specific fakes reported, but sibling LME49720/LM4562 fakes are well documented on diyAudio. Obsolete since 2017, so marketplace SOIC/TO-99 units carry remark risk. Check marking, date code and can finish; bench-test bias current, slew and distortion.

claims_confirmed: Farnell copy is the National-format datasheet dated May 21, 2010 (https://www.farnell.com/datasheets/577866.pdf).
Octopart copy is the National-format LME49713HA datasheet dated June 2, 2010 (https://datasheet.octopart.com/LME49713HA-National-Semiconductor-datasheet-15941891.pdf).
Supply ±5 V to ±18 V, noise 1.9 nV/√Hz, THD+N 0.00036% (https://media.digikey.com/pdf/Data%20Sheets/Texas%20Instruments%20PDFs/LME49713.pdf).
Slew ±1900 V/µs, output ±100 mA, bandwidth 132 MHz, closed-loop bandwidth set by feedback resistor (https://www.farnell.com/datasheets/577866.pdf).
LME49713MA/NOPB obsolete; LME49713MAX/NOPB is the alternate packaging (https://www.digikey.com/en/products/detail/texas-instruments/LME49713MA-NOPB/1836036).
Head-Fi thread 'LME49713, could be a killer opamp' exists (https://www.head-fi.org/threads/lme49713-could-be-a-killer-opamp.267524/).
diyAudio user: ran hot or oscillated in Sony CDP-557ESD NE5534 sockets; AD844 worked (https://www.diyaudio.com/community/threads/lme49713-opamp-problem.151403/).
Forum: SO-8 single only, so NE5532 DIP sockets need adapters; no capacitor across the feedback resistor (https://www.diyaudio.com/forums/analog-line-level/330762-lme49713.html).
